alerts.title: EFV neuropsychiatric side effects: insomnia and vivid dreams
alerts.message: Guidelines list insomnia as a recognized toxicity requiring management. For patients on EFV 600mg, the recommended action is to lower the dose to EFV 400mg. If already on EFV 400mg and symptoms persist, substitute EFV with DTG. The patient has been on EFV-based ART since February 2024 and presents with poor sleep and vivid dreams for several weeks. These symptoms are well-known EFV neuropsychiatric effects. Evidence for drug attribution includes the classic symptom profile and temporal relationship to ongoing EFV use. Evidence against includes the absence of other EFV-related symptoms such as dizziness or seizures, and possible non-drug causes of insomnia. The clinician's plan documents the complaints but does not include any guideline-recommended management step.

evidence.recommended_action: If on EFV 600mg, reduce to EFV 400mg. If already on EFV 400mg and symptoms persist, substitute EFV with DTG. If DTG contraindicated, use ATV/r.

alerts.title: Viral load monitoring overdue per guideline schedule
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend routine viral load monitoring at 6 months and 12 months after ART initiation, then every 12 months for adults. The patient started ART in February 2024, so 6-month and 12-month VL checks should have occurred around August 2024 and February 2025. The only VL on record is from August 2025 (60 copies/mL, suppressed). The next annual VL would be due around August 2026. However, the most recent VL was approximately 165 days before the current visit, placing it within the expected annual window. No monitoring gap is identified for the current visit date.

evidence.recommended_action: Continue routine annual viral load monitoring. Next VL due approximately August 2026 based on last test date.
